title: State conviction concludes child sex case - NewsBreak
text:
By CONTRIBUTED REPORT ,
5 hours ago
MARATHON — The Monroe County State Attorney's Office recently announced the culmination of child sex charges against a former Marathon couple.
On Aug. 18, Circuit Judge Mark Jones found Eric Cadogan, 41, guilty on state charges of incest, sexual battery on a person under age 12, lewd or lascivious molestation, contributing to the delinquency or dependency of a child, promoting sexual performance by a child, sexual battery on a helpless person and neglect of a child causing great bodily harm.
Cadogan is currently serving a 20-year federal prison sentence in a separate child exploitation case. Upon completion of that term, he will be remanded to the Florida Department of Corrections to serve a 20-year state prison sentence.
Investigators determined that the criminal activities had been occurring for a significant period of time. During the course of earlier proceedings, state social services intervened and Cadogan, along with his wife, Kia Lynn Cadogan, lost custody of their children due to abuse and neglect.
Eric Cadogan's prosecution was directly tied to the case of Kia Lynn Cadogan, 37, who cooperated in the investigation and was sentenced earlier this year to 13 years in state prison, followed by 13 years of probation for incest, sexual battery and child neglect.
Despite the reduced sentence based on her cooperation, she will remain on Florida’s sexual predator registry for life — a designation that requires lifetime reporting, monitoring and strict supervision under state law.
“This is one of the most appalling cases ever prosecuted in Monroe County,” State Attorney Dennis Ward said. “Children should never be subjected to this kind of depravity — least of all by their own parents. What Eric and Kia Cadogan did is beyond disgraceful; it is inhuman. Florida has delivered justice, and both will pay with long years in prison.”
